title: Japan 2026 Logistics Occupier Survey
summary: CBRE's 2026 Logistics Occupier Survey, conducted in March 2026, finds that Japanese logistics occupiers are increasingly focused on attracting and retaining staff and improving operational efficiency. A mandatory Chief Logistics Officer (CLO) appointment requirement under the revised Act on Advancement of Integration and Streamlining of Distribution Business, effective April 2026, is expected to accelerate efficiency measures. Appetite for relocation and expansion remains robust, with some occupiers renewing contracts multiple times at the same facility.

title: 2026 Asia Pacific Data Centre Trends & Outlook
summary: The Asia Pacific data centre market continues to experience an unprecedented boom, with demand expanding rapidly on the back of AI implementation, cloud adoption, and digitalisation. Global hyperscale demand is growing at a CAGR of 14%, and tech firms plan to increase CapEx on AI by 61% in 2026. Direct investment volume reached a record high of US$11.6 billion in 2025, with neocloud providers emerging as a new demand driver; power availability and elevated construction costs remain the two most pressing challenges to expansion.

title: Hong Kong Residential Insights May 2026
summary: Hong Kong's residential property market recorded a significant broad-based rebound in April 2026, with total home sales value jumping 50.9% YoY to HK$63.7 billion and transaction volume rising 29.4% YoY to 7,368 units. The luxury segment surged with 87 units priced above HK$100 million transacted as of mid-April, representing approximately 135% YoY growth. CBRE projects full-year 2026 residential prices to rise approximately 8% to 10%, supported by easing supply pressures and developer confidence.

title: Japan Viewpoint: Shifting Domestic Consumption Patterns to Boost Demand for High Street Stores
summary: This viewpoint examines how shifting domestic consumption patterns in Japan are expected to generate stronger demand for high street retail space. CBRE notes that supply-demand conditions remain extremely tight, with several of the nine surveyed high street areas posting vacancy rates of 0%. Rents have exceeded pre-pandemic peaks in seven of the nine surveyed areas, and CBRE projects Ginza high street rents to reach JPY 299,500 per tsubo by end-2027.
prime_rent: Ginza high street rent projected to reach JPY 299,500/tsubo by end-2027

title: 2025 Tokyo Flexible Office Market
summary: The Tokyo flexible office market grew moderately by 5.0% YoY in 2025, with flexible space accounting for 3.3% of the total Tokyo office market. Operators are increasingly selecting high-grade buildings with strong amenities to support talent attraction and flexible work styles, with the share of new openings in Tokyo's five central wards increasing. Companies using flexible office space have been more successful in talent recruitment, and firms planning to increase usage significantly outnumber those planning to reduce it.

title: Japan Investment MarketView Q1 2026
summary: Commercial real estate investment volume in Japan increased 2% YoY to a record first-quarter high of JPY 2.043 trillion in Q1 2026, with overseas investors completing a large-scale acquisition exceeding JPY 100 billion. The residential, logistics, and hotel sectors each recorded double-digit YoY volume growth, while hotel investment reached a record quarterly high. Expected NOI yields for Tokyo prime office assets in Otemachi rose 2 bps QoQ to 3.15%.
prime_yield: Tokyo prime office (Otemachi) expected NOI yield: 3.15%

title: Japan Retail MarketView Q1 2026
summary: Average rents set new all-time highs in five of the ten surveyed high street areas in Q1 2026 — Ginza, Omotesando/Harajuku, Shibuya, Shinsaibashi, and Kyoto — driven by fashion sector demand and new brand store openings. Vacancy in both Ginza and Shibuya remained at 0.0%, reflecting extremely tight supply conditions. Multiple retailers competing for single available units has become increasingly common, and CBRE expects average rents to continue on an upward trend.
prime_rent: Ginza and Shibuya vacancy at 0.0%; rents at new all-time highs in these markets

title: Asia Pacific Figures Q1 2026
summary: Asia Pacific commercial real estate investment volume fell 9% QoQ to US$46.2 billion in Q1 2026, pulling back from the prior quarter's record high, but was up 18% YoY on an annual basis. Asia-wide Grade A office net absorption totalled 17.3 million sq. ft. NFA, up 7.8% QoQ and broadly on track with 2025 levels, with occupier sentiment remaining resilient despite the onset of the Middle East conflict. Logistics leasing momentum slowed in Q1 2026 after a relatively robust previous quarter.

title: The Leasing Gauge 2026
summary: CBRE's Leasing Gauge 2026 report for Australia examines commercial real estate leasing conditions across key property sectors, noting that supply constraints are intensifying across markets and rent growth is tracking above expectations. The report highlights that economic rents continue to sit 20-30% above market rents as construction costs remain elevated, favouring a buy-over-build strategy. Both office and retail sectors are showing stronger leasing fundamentals than anticipated at the start of the year.

title: Retail Built to Endure: The Resilience of Australian Shopping Centres
summary: Australian shopping centres are delivering income stability in uncertain markets, benefiting from strong population growth, limited new supply, and improved tenant economics that position retail as a defensive asset class with resilient income-led returns. Shopping centre rents are forecast to rise in the mid-single digit range in 2026, with Perth outperforming and vacancy rates remaining below 5% across most submarkets. Development costs and land prices are constraining new supply pipelines, further underpinning the outlook for existing assets.
prime_rent: Shopping centre rents forecast to rise mid-single digits in 2026; Sydney and Perth pacing at +7% YoY

title: Japan Logistics MarketView Q1 2026
summary: The Greater Tokyo logistics vacancy rate decreased 0.6 pp QoQ to 9.2% in Q1 2026, with net absorption significantly surpassing the five-year quarterly average on strong demand for existing properties; effective rents rose 0.9% QoQ to JPY 4,530. Greater Osaka saw the vacancy rate fall sharply by 1.5 pp to 2.2%, with three new properties completing at full occupancy and effective rents rising 1.2% QoQ to JPY 4,350. Greater Nagoya vacancy increased to 16.8%, though effective rents still rose marginally to JPY 3,740.

title: Japan Office MarketView Q1 2026
summary: Tokyo's All-Grade office vacancy rate fell 0.1 pp QoQ to 1.5% in Q1 2026, with net absorption of 114,000 tsubo surpassing the new supply of 103,000 tsubo; Grade A and Grade A- rents both recorded their second-highest QoQ growth rates on record. In Osaka, the All-Grade vacancy rate declined to 2.0%, with Grade B rents surging 3.9% QoQ to JPY 16,150 — surpassing the previous peak set in Q1 2008. All-Grade rents rose in nine of the ten surveyed regional cities, with Sapporo, Saitama, Hiroshima, and Fukuoka continuing to set record highs.

title: Australia Retail Figures Q1 2026
summary: Net face rents grew across all retail sectors in Australia in Q1 2026, with CBD secondary and super prime assets recording the highest growth of 2.3% and 2.2% QoQ respectively. Shopping centre and large format yields continued to compress, with large format centres compressing 4 bps QoQ, while there were 32 retail transactions exceeding A$5 million totalling c.A$1.67 billion. Consumer sentiment declined significantly, with the Westpac-Melbourne Institute Index falling 12.5% to 80.1 in April amid global uncertainty.

title: Hong Kong Viewpoint: Recovery Time – How Financial Sector Demand is Reviving Hong Kong's Grade A Office Market
summary: Strong capital market performance, increasing wealth inflows, and supportive government policies are reinforcing Hong Kong's status as a leading global financial hub and underpinning a rebound in office leasing demand, predominantly in the Central CBD. Financial sector demand — particularly from wealth management, insurance, and non-bank financial firms — is driving a sustained recovery in Central Grade A office rents and absorbing vacancy. CBRE identifies the financial sector as the key structural driver of Hong Kong's office market revival in 2026.

title: Asia Pacific Office Trends Q1 2026
summary: Asia Pacific office leasing was broadly unaffected by the onset of the Middle East conflict in Q1 2026, though several Southeast Asian markets implemented work-from-home policies to reduce energy and fuel demand. Singapore's office market carried its positive momentum into 2026, underpinned by strong occupier demand and record-low vacancy, with the banking and financial sector — led by wealth management, hedge funds, and quant trading firms — remaining the key demand driver. Tokyo's office market remains exceptionally tight due to robust domestic demand, with more landlords incorporating CPI-linked clauses in lease contracts for annual rental adjustments.

title: Asia Pacific Industrial & Logistics Trends Q1 2026
summary: Recent oil price volatility has emerged as a key risk for the Asia Pacific industrial and logistics market, with higher transport costs and supply chain disruption weighing on occupier demand, though traditional 3PL operators continued to underpin leasing activity in Q1 2026. In Australia, 3PL operators are consolidating from older second-generation facilities into new super prime assets, while renewals drive the bulk of leasing activity due to tight availability and elevated fit-out costs. Japan's Greater Tokyo logistics market continues to recover from previous supply spikes with overall vacancy trending downward, while Greater Osaka saw robust leasing supported by domestic consumption.

title: Talking Property – The House View Q2 2026
summary: CBRE Australia's Head of Research Sameer Chopra and Phil Rowland discuss the rapidly shifting economic and geopolitical landscape, noting that office prime effective rents grew 8% YoY in Brisbane and Sydney — far ahead of year-start expectations — and industrial net effective rents declined approximately 2.5% in Sydney and Melbourne due to elevated incentives amid new supply. CBRE now expects transaction volumes to grow approximately 5% in 2026 (revised down from 10%), with cap rate expansion of 10-15 bps in office, 25-35 bps in industrial, and 10-15 bps in shopping centres. Supply constraints are intensifying across all sectors as construction cost forecasts have risen materially.
prime_yield: Office cap rate expansion: 10-15 bps; industrial: 25-35 bps; shopping centres: 10-15 bps in 2026
prime_rent: Office: Sydney +8% YoY, Brisbane +8% YoY, Perth +5%, Melbourne +3%; Retail: Sydney/Perth regional centres +7% YoY; Industrial: Sydney/Melbourne net effective rents -2.5%

title: Seoul Figures Q1 2026
summary: Average Grade A office vacancy across Seoul's three major business districts declined to 2.8% in Q1 2026, stabilising the market, though new leasing volume fell both QoQ and YoY amid a wait-and-see stance ahead of anticipated Q2 CBD completions. Logistics supply in 2026 is forecast at a decade low, driving vacancy to continue declining from its 2024 peak with dry storage vacancy falling below 10%, while 3PL and e-commerce tenants accounted for 65% of new take-up. Overall Seoul investment volume declined 17% YoY, though strategic investor-led office acquisitions and selective prime logistics transactions continued.

title: Brisbane CBD Office Figures Q1 2026
summary: Brisbane CBD prime gross face rents grew 3.7% QoQ and 9.2% YoY in Q1 2026, among the strongest performances in Australia, with incentives declining 50 bps to average 38.9%. Prime CBD yields tightened slightly by 2 bps to 7.02%, reflecting late 2025 transaction activity. Market sentiment is noticeably improved year-on-year, with more tenants engaging with the market, though rising bond rates and the cash rate are creating some near-term investment uncertainty.

title: Australia CBD Office Figures Q1 2026
summary: Australian CBD prime effective rents climbed 1.8% QoQ and 6.6% YoY in Q1 2026, the highest annual growth since early 2019, driven by the lowest new supply pipeline in over 30 years and improving leasing sentiment. Prime yields were stable at an average of 6.67% across Australian CBDs, with transaction activity reaching A$3.5 billion — a solid start to the year despite global headwinds from the Middle East conflict. No new office space was delivered to the Sydney CBD in 2026, and development is set to slow substantially going forward.

No new office space will be delivered to the Sydney CBD in 2026, and all four major precincts — Core, Midtown, Walsh Bay, and Western Corridor — recorded strong prime net effective rent growth. Investment volumes reached A$1.1 billion in the Sydney CBD in Q1 2026, with cap rates held stable despite global headwinds.

No new supply was delivered this quarter, and with positive net absorption of 375,400 sq. ft. (a fourth consecutive positive quarter), overall vacancy fell 0.4 pp to 16.8%, the biggest single-quarter decline since Q2 2015. Low vacancy in prime areas pushed high street shop rents up 0.9% QoQ — the fifteenth consecutive quarterly increase — with vacancy for core retail districts rising slightly to 6.8%, still near its lowest since early 2024. Mainland Chinese tea and coffee shops continued to expand across the market.

Despite positive net absorption of 135,800 sq. ft. — ending four consecutive quarters of net withdrawal — overall warehouse rents fell a further 1.2% QoQ as landlords cut rates to improve occupancy, marking the ninth consecutive quarterly rental decline. Overall warehouse vacancy narrowed slightly by 0.3 pp to 12.8%.

End-users were the dominant buyers at 43% of total volume, with 14 of the 29 transactions involving financially stressed assets totalling HK$8.7 billion. Hotel investment gained traction as institutional investors targeted student hostel conversions.

title: Australia Industrial and Logistics Figures Q1 2026

National super prime midpoint yields expanded marginally to 5.7%, reflecting higher interest rates and elevated bond yields, while effective rents returned to growth as face rental growth began to offset elevated incentives. Close to 40% of the 2026-2027 supply pipeline is pre-committed, with investment sales for income-producing assets totalling close to A$1 billion.

Transaction volume growth expectations for 2026 were reduced, with total returns shifting away from cap rate compression towards rent growth. Construction costs are forecast to grow 18% between 2026 and 2027, further constraining future supply pipelines.

The report highlights resilient occupier demand, flight-to-quality trends in office markets, and strong RevPAR growth in APAC hotels.

Japan led at USD 13.2 billion, Singapore surged 433% to USD 11.5 billion (driven by mega-fund asset transfers), Australia recorded USD 5.7 billion (+49% YoY), Hong Kong rose 41% to USD 1.6 billion, and South Korea reached USD 4.8 billion. Cross-border capital flows hit an all-time quarterly high of USD 16.3 billion, up 87% YoY.

The sector outlook remains supported by continual investor demand for quality logistics assets and Singapore's attractiveness as a safe investment haven.

title: Singapore Retail Market Update Q1 2026
summary: Islandwide retail occupancy held steady in Q1 2026 despite several high-profile store closures, with vacancies quickly backfilled by new and existing brands. The retail sector continues to benefit from strong household spending, tourism recovery, and the flight of shoppers back to prime malls and street-level retail. Supply constraints continue to underpin rental stability in well-located assets.

title: Singapore Residential Market Update Q1 2026
summary: Private home prices rose at a faster pace in Q1 2026, though overall sales activity softened. Rental prices rebounded marginally from a 0.5% QoQ drop in Q4 2025 to a 0.3% increase in Q1 2026. Executive Condominiums were the standout performer, with transaction volume tripling to approximately 1,500 units, while District 10 median prices surged over 40% driven by large-format freehold resale demand.
primeRent: +0.3% QoQ residential rents in Q1 2026

title: Singapore Auction Market Update Q1 2026
summary: Knight Frank's quarterly Singapore Auction Market Update for Q1 2026 reports on the performance of residential and commercial property auctions in Singapore. The report covers auction volumes, hammer rates, and key transactions across both residential and commercial sectors, providing insights into distressed and voluntary auction activity in the current market environment.

title: Mixed-use Developments: Conduits to Quality Living — Singapore
summary: This Singapore thought leadership report examines how larger mixed-use units are outpacing smaller ones on price growth, and how offices are increasingly choosing to buy rather than lease as part of a broader shift toward the 'Third Place' model that integrates offices, homes and communities under one development. The report reflects evolving tenant and owner preferences for amenity-rich, live-work-play environments.

title: Leading Indicators — May 2026
summary: Knight Frank's monthly Leading Indicators report tracks key economic and financial metrics impacting property markets across the Asia-Pacific region and globally. Published by Chief Economist Ben Burston, the May 2026 edition covers macro indicators including interest rates, inflation, GDP growth trajectories, and real estate capital flows relevant to investment decision-making across APAC markets.

title: Leading Indicators — April 2026
summary: Knight Frank's monthly Leading Indicators report for April 2026 tracks key economic and financial metrics impacting property markets globally and across Asia-Pacific. Published by Chief Economist Ben Burston, the report covers macro drivers including interest rate dynamics, inflation trends, GDP growth, and capital flow signals relevant to APAC real estate markets.

title: The Wealth Report 2026
summary: Knight Frank's 20th annual Wealth Report finds the global UHNW population reached 713,626 in 2026, with Asia-Pacific holding nearly 31% of the total. Tokyo led the PIRI 100 Prime International Residential Index with a 58.5% surge in prime residential prices in 2025, while Singapore's UHNW population is forecast to grow 46% by 2031 and Brisbane is identified as a next-tier global luxury market driven by the 2032 Olympics infrastructure pipeline. Australia's billionaire population is forecast to grow 77% over five years.
primeRent: Tokyo prime new-build: +58.5% in 2025; Hong Kong prime: -2.1% in 2025; Singapore luxury residential: +7.9% in 2025

title: Data Centres Global Report 2026
summary: Knight Frank's global data centre report covers the rapidly expanding sector shaped by AI, hyperscale demand, and new financing models. The report forecasts data centre capacity growth of almost 25% over the next two years globally, with over 80% of 2026 APAC capacity already pre-let. Japan has seen the largest-ever data centre financing deal in the country, and the report notes US$15 billion invested in APAC data centres in 2025 alone.

title: Powering Property and Private Capital — Data Centre AI Infrastructure Analysis
summary: AI-driven data centre demand is creating one of the most capital-intensive development cycles in real estate history, with the IEA projecting global electricity demand from data centres to more than double to ~950 TWh by 2030. Knight Frank forecasts data centre capacity growth of almost 25% over the next two years, with $1.4–1.6 trillion of infrastructure investment required over five years. APAC is a key growth region with Japan, Singapore and Australia among the leading markets.

title: Asia-Pacific Capital Markets Insights — Japan Focus Q1 2026
summary: Japan attracted US$6 billion in inbound capital in Q1 2026 — 43% above the 10-year quarterly average — driven by tight prime office vacancy and stable leasing demand. Tokyo office rents rose 22% YoY as Grade A vacancy approached near-zero levels, while retail rents rose 8%. Living sector volumes dominated at over 80% of APAC living investment in Q1 2026, and data centre demand is rapidly expanding with over 80% of 2026 capacity already pre-let.
primeRent: Tokyo office: +22% YoY; Tokyo retail: +8% YoY

title: Asia-Pacific Capital Markets Insights — South Korea Focus Q1 2026
summary: South Korea ranked third for APAC cross-border investment inflows in Q1 2026, with volumes rising 45.0% year-on-year to US$1.4 billion. Logistics assets accounted for 38.8% of activity, reflecting steady demand and moderating supply, with KKR's acquisition of the Shinsegae Food Hub for US$201.1 million as the headline deal. Office investment is stabilising after meaningful repricing, with domestic Korean capital dominating Seoul office activity.

title: Prime International Residential Index (PIRI 100) — 2025 Annual Results
summary: The PIRI 100 recorded 3.2% average price growth across 100 tracked luxury markets in 2025, with 73 markets seeing increases. Asia-Pacific averaged 3.6% growth, with Tokyo leading globally at +58.5% driven by yen weakness and prime supply scarcity. Hong Kong recorded a -2.1% annual decline in prime prices, though super-prime activity surged with 81 US$10 million+ transactions in Q4 2025. The report is published as part of The Wealth Report 2026.
primeRent: Tokyo: +58.5%; Hong Kong: -2.1%; APAC average: +3.6% (all in 2025)

title: APAC Prime Residential Markets Diverge — Wealth Report 2026 Analysis
summary: Knight Frank analysis published May 2026 highlights widening divergence in APAC prime residential markets. Tokyo led all global luxury markets at +58.5% in 2025, while Greater China markets remained under pressure with Guangzhou down 12.2% and Hong Kong slipping 2.1%. Singapore's UHNW population is forecast to grow 46% by 2031 with luxury residential prices up 7.9% in 2025. Australia's billionaire population is forecast to grow 77% over five years.
primeRent: Tokyo: +58.5%; Singapore luxury residential: +7.9% (2025)

title: APAC Real Estate Investment Q1 2026 — Capital Markets Analysis
summary: APAC real estate investment reached US$64.6 billion in Q1 2026, the strongest quarterly result since Q4 2021, as capital decisively shifted from price discovery to deployment. Cross-border volumes more than doubled YoY to US$22.4 billion, with sovereign wealth funds and institutional investors deploying US$12.8 billion combined (+50% YoY). Japan topped inbound capital attraction at US$6 billion, with Singapore cross-border volumes surging to US$5.7 billion from under US$1 billion a year earlier.

title: Australian Horizon Report 2026
summary: Knight Frank's Australian Horizon Report for 2026 examines the outlook for Australian real estate across residential, commercial and alternative sectors. The report identifies Australia as a stable, mature market for cross-border investors with billionaire wealth forecast to grow 77% over five years. Brisbane is highlighted as a next-tier global luxury market driven by the 2032 Olympics, infrastructure investment, and wealth migration from interstate.

title: Asia-Pacific Q1 2026 Office Highlights — Australia Focus
summary: Knight Frank's APAC Office Highlights found Australia and India are leading the regional office recovery, with annual prime net face rent growth in Sydney at 8.6% and Brisbane at 8.2% — the second and third strongest rates in APAC after Bengaluru and Tokyo respectively. APAC-wide prime net face rents rose 0.8% in Q1 2026, with 18 of 24 monitored cities recording stable or increasing rents despite geopolitical uncertainty.
primeRent: Sydney: +8.6% YoY prime net face rent; Brisbane: +8.2% YoY

title: Central Leads Hong Kong Island Office Recovery — Q1 2026
summary: Premium Central continued to outperform the broader Hong Kong office market with 5.1% QoQ rental growth in Q1 2026, with Traditional Central and Admiralty also rising 5.7% and 2.6% respectively. Finance sector demand — particularly from traditional securities houses, asset management firms, and Middle Eastern banks — drove the recovery. Knight Frank expects leasing momentum to strengthen further in Q2 2026, broadening beyond Premium Central to include Traditional Central, Admiralty and Wan Chai.
primeRent: Premium Central: +5.1% QoQ; Traditional Central: +5.7% QoQ; Admiralty: +2.6% QoQ

title: Singapore Investment Market Q1 2026 — Record First Quarter
summary: Singapore logged S$15.4 billion in real estate investment sales in Q1 2026, a new first-quarter record representing a 166.5% YoY and 10% QoQ increase. The strong performance was driven by a low interest rate environment and key deals including Asia Square Tower 1's injection into a private fund (~S$4.1 billion), sale of 78 Shenton Way (~S$615 million), and Bukit Panjang Plaza's divestment (S$428 million). Knight Frank maintained its full-year 2026 forecast at approximately S$30 billion.

title: Singapore Investment Market Update Q1 2026 (Full Report)
summary: Knight Frank Singapore's comprehensive Q1 2026 Investment Market Update reports on investment sales reaching S$15.4 billion — the highest first-quarter figure on record. Commercial property led all sectors with S$6.3 billion in transactions despite a 17.2% QoQ decline, while industrial activity rose sharply to S$3.1 billion. Outbound investment from Singapore rose 7.8% QoQ to S$10.3 billion as entities sought stable markets and income resilience.

title: Australian Retail Review — April 2026 (Detailed Analysis)
summary: Australia's retail property sector delivered the strongest total return of all commercial property sectors in 2025 at 9.2% — the best result since 2017 — supported by years of subdued development activity and rising tenant turnover. Around A$3.6 billion of retail transactions occurred in Q1 2026. Despite near-term uncertainty from the Middle East conflict, medium-term fundamentals remain supportive given a constrained development pipeline, elevated construction costs, and limited new supply feasibility.
